Project owner, Glessner House version 4 reconstruction brief, 29 September 2026: correct intersecting roofs, courtyard and garden-level openings, continuous copper roof at the inner northeast corner, variable-height ashlar courses, and east-wing chimneys. Follow-up 1 October 2026: rebuild west-wing roof, gables and dormer from northwest/west views; carve the north entrance alcove with left-turn steps and door against HABS floor plans. Later 1 October correction: continuous rear ridge, balanced solid south gable and courtyard eave matching the north range. Follow-up 2 October 2026: correct north windows protruding through the eave; rebuild the whole west elevation to the supplied square-on reconstruction, including stone courses, openings, low rear roof, hood, gutters and turret-to-gable alignment; assess north stone appendage and doors. Follow-up 7 October 2026: remove the recessed cuts beside the courtyard dining tower; connect its copper hip to the north roof with raised tiled slopes and matching ridge adornment. Follow-up 8 October 2026: raise the courtyard dining-tower upper glazing to align with the north-wing upper windows, shortening the copper cap while retaining period-appropriate sash divisions. Follow-up 9 October 2026 UTC: correct the front west gable angle and rear section width against the supplied west and northwest images, then validate against both photographs before merging to dev. Later 9 October correction: restore the west wing's full-height level ridge, simple front and rear gables, and matching courtyard awning; the lowered rear roof and exposed courtyard wall are a regression. Follow-up15October2026: prioritize a straight north-wing ridge through the west-wing junction, move the west peak to achieve a right-angle intersection, and compare the remaining roof features and northeast copper coverage against the supplied overhead views. Follow-up16October2026: photograph-match the Prairie entry lower side reveals, shaped header, one inset step and recessed decorative field; distinguish the recessed entrance from lower stones that slope outward.
